docs.home.title: Documentation
docs.home.description: Guides and API notes for building long-lived, state-heavy browser applications with MotifJS.
docs.code.preferenceHint: Examples on every page follow this choice.
meta.title: MotifJS — For long-lived browser applications
meta.description: MotifJS is a JavaScript and TypeScript UI framework for long-lived, state-heavy browser applications.
about.title: About MotifJS
about.description: MotifJS is built for long-lived, state-heavy browser applications. It runs in the browser and does not provide server-side rendering.
home.hero.description: MotifJS is a JavaScript and TypeScript UI framework for browser applications that stay active across long sessions. Components, routing, and lifecycle-aware cleanup are part of the core.
home.preview.articleDescription: Choose the way you like to write MotifJS. The same idea, in your preferred style.
home.preview.note: Subscriptions are released when their component is disposed.
home.value.description: MotifJS is intended for state-heavy browser applications: tools where users keep context while data and interface state change around them.
home.feature1.title: Keep a live interface in sync
home.feature1.description: Reactive objects and bindings connect application state to the text, attributes, and lists that use it. Updates follow those dependencies.
home.feature1.caption: Reactive bindings, no VDOM diff
home.feature2.title: Treat lifecycles as part of the app
home.feature2.description: Components have configuration, mount, activation, and disposal hooks. Register timers and subscriptions for cleanup with their owner.
home.feature2.caption: Lifecycle and cleanup built in
home.feature3.title: Choose your component form
home.feature3.description: Write components as a class, a function, or an Options-style object. The three forms use the same component model.
home.feature3.caption: Class · Function · Options
home.approach.kicker: Two ways to build a component
home.approach.description: Use a returned view for declarative structure, or manage controls imperatively when you need direct control. The two approaches can coexist in one application.
home.approach.card1Title:
Use JSX for structure.
Add controls when needed.
home.approach.card1Description: Declare the component view with JSX, then use the controls collection to add or move elements at runtime.
home.approach.card2Title:
Three component forms.
One consistent model.
home.approach.card2Description: Keep a component lightweight or give it a full lifecycle—without changing how the framework behaves.
home.approach.card3Title:
Update the part
that depends on state.
home.approach.card3Description: The compiler turns reactive reads into bindings. A state change updates its dependent DOM value rather than rebuilding the whole component.
home.runtime.description: MotifJS mounts into the browser DOM. It includes routing, component lifecycle hooks, and disposal tools for applications that continue working after the initial load.
home.runtime.point3: Clean up component-owned work on dispose
home.runtime.ssrNote: MotifJS does not provide server-side rendering (SSR). If a page must arrive as server-rendered HTML, use an SSR-capable framework.
home.runtime.visualLabel: A reactive state value updates its bound DOM node
home.explore.description: Components, routes, shared services, and reactivity are part of the same application model.
home.explore.reactivityDescription: Use reactive objects, signals, and bindings to connect application state with the parts of the interface that use it.
home.explore.routingDescription: Layouts, nested routes, and a built-in RouterView.
home.explore.servicesDescription: Use dependency injection or a reactive store.
home.explore.lifecycleDescription: Register timers and subscriptions with a component so they are released when it is disposed.
home.explore.virtualizationDescription: Keep long collections manageable by rendering the rows around the current viewport.
home.explore.examplesDescription: See one idea expressed as Declarative or Imperative code, using Class, Function, or Options components.
home.principles.titleEnd: A few ways to use it.
home.principles.stat3Detail: One model across all three forms
home.community.kicker: Open source, built in the open
home.community.description: Explore the source, follow development, or share the patterns you discover as you build.
home.start.description: Install the runtime and compiler. Then create a component and decide what should live for the duration of the session.
